主要内容: In early 2009, Christopher Nassetta, then CEO of Hilton Worldwide Holdings, faced significant challenges as the recession deepened. His efforts to turnaround the iconic hotel company, founded by Paris Hilton’s great-grandfather, had turned into a nightmare. After closing Hilton’s Beverly Hills headquarters, Nassetta returned to the East Coast, where he faced further difficulties. The situation eventually led to Blackstone's $26 billion acquisition of Hilton, marking one of the largest leveraged buyouts in history. This deal, announced in 2014, highlighted the complexities of corporate restructuring during economic downturns and the strategic moves by private equity firms to capitalize on distressed assets.
